Q: How to retrieve PID from windows event log? A:

Win32_NTLogEvent WMI class mirrors the EVENTLOGRECORD structure from the older Event Log API. The XML representation that you see in "XML View" is only available through the Vista Event Log API e.g. as per Get an event object from win32evtlog.EvtQuery results :

import lxml.objectify
import win32evtlog

hevq=win32evtlog.EvtQuery("System",win32evtlog.EvtQueryReverseDirection,'*[System[Level=2]]')
while hh:=win32evtlog.EvtNext(hevq,1):
  hev=hh[0]
  x=win32evtlog.EvtRender(hev, win32evtlog.EvtRenderEventXml)
  o=lxml.objectify.fromstring(x)
  # will raise an exception if not found
  print(o.System.Execution.attrib['ProcessID'])

Note that event properties are specific to each event (or more likely, to the combination of provider and event ID). While possible <System> subelements are constrained by the Event schema (specifically, the SystemPropertiesType Complex Type), most of them are optional (use="optional" for attributes, minOccurs="0" for elements in the schema).

Q: Right align texts in Canvas using Jetpack Compose A:

You measure the text based on the string characters only. But when you actually display the text you modify its size, so the calculation using the TextMeasurer is off.

Simply also include the style in the calculation, and everything works out:

val yAxisLabelMaxWidth = textMeasurer.measure(text = "${max.toInt()}", style = style).size.width.toFloat()
val yAxisLabelMinWidth = textMeasurer.measure(text = "${min.toInt()}", style = style).size.width.toFloat()

For that you should extract the style into a dedicated variable to prevent writing the same piece of code four times:

val style = TextStyle(
    fontSize = 10.sp,
    background = Color.Green,
)

You should probably do the same for the texts.
